AIChatApp Troubleshooting Reference

When chat is slow:
- Large prompt context increases latency.
- Broad documentation stuffing makes short prompts perform worse.
- Streaming may be limited by client timeout, gateway timeout, or model speed.

When a response is cut off:
- ask-continue is used to finish the missing final part.
- Incomplete responses can come from max token limits or stop conditions.

When chat returns 401 invalid_token:
- The browser may be using a stale JWT.
- Login may have happened against one running instance while chat is routed to another.
- JwtSettings may differ across environments.
- In local Web development, Frontend:GatewayBaseUrl should use https://localhost:7067/ instead of http://localhost:5031/ so Authorization: Bearer tokens are not lost during Gateway HTTPS redirection.
- Restart API, Gateway, and Web after changing auth or gateway config, then sign in again.

When the UI says the session expired immediately after login:
- Check AIChatApp.Web/appsettings.Development.json and confirm Frontend:GatewayBaseUrl is https://localhost:7067/.
- Check API logs for LocalJwt authentication failure details.
- Confirm Gateway routes auth and chat to the same API instance.

When Docker compose reports mssqlserver conflict:
- Another SQL Server container with that name already exists.
- Reuse the existing SQL container instead of creating a new one.

When SSE writes throw TaskCanceledException:
- The client likely disconnected or the request was canceled mid-stream.

When documentation answers look wrong:
- Check README.md
- Check the assistant FAQ and the focused assistant knowledge files
- Check appsettings and launchSettings
- Check the current implementation in code
